properties.name: The agent never authors a design artifact that requires professional licensure or accountable sign-off — it carries the requirement into the tool and the result back as evidence
properties.statement:
Where a design artifact carries PROFESSIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY — a stamped structural drawing, a permit submission, a certified analysis, a safety or medical certification — the agent must not produce it. It may state the requirement the artifact has to meet, identify who or what produces it, and record the returned result as a Verification with its provenance. It must not be the author.

Anthony, 2026-08-30, accepting this after a brainstorm on non-software domains (`dec:idea-who-authors-the-domain-artifact`, where this was tier 3 of three).

⭐ THE REASON IS NOT AGENT QUALITY, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A GUIDELINE. The other two tiers turn on whether a human can review the output, which is a judgement that moves as models improve. This one does not move at all: in most jurisdictions a structural drawing for a habitable structure is stamped by a licensed engineer, and an analysis someone relies on is a professional judgement with a name attached to it. No level of model competence makes an unlicensed author licensed. A better agent makes tiers 1 and 2 wider; it leaves this boundary exactly where it is.

DISTINGUISH IT FROM THE FABRICATION RULE IT SITS BESIDE. `cap:no-fabricated-repair` and the viewpoints no-extrapolation rule both stop the agent inventing content nobody stated — they answer "did anybody decide this?". This answers a different question: "is this agent ENTITLED to be the one who says it?" An artifact can be entirely faithful to the design, invent nothing, and still be one the agent must not sign.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: that reflow2 cannot help with such a design. It can hold the requirements, the interfaces, the allocations and the verification matrix for a permitted building all the way through — and that is most of the work. What it must not do is emit the document that carries somebody's professional signature.

CONCRETE CASES BEHIND IT: a garage extension needing a permit (Alex's, the nearest real candidate), and a car-engine component whose FEA under thermal and cyclic loading somebody is accountable for.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how the boundary is DETECTED rather than merely stated. Nothing in reflow2 today knows which artifact types carry licensure, and jurisdictions differ. A requirement with no detector behind it is the weakest of the three legs — so this is accepted intent with its enforcement still open.
